newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Defence asks Ethiopian court to dismiss charges.
newsitem.headline: Defence asks Ethiopian court to dismiss charges.

text.p: Defence lawyers asked an Ethiopian court on Wednesday to dismiss corruption charges against a former deputy prime minister and eight other accused and set them free.
The lawyers for former deputy prime minister Tamirat Layne and the eight others said they were being prosecuted under a defunct law which was passed in 1982 to protect Marxist military rule.
Tamirat, who is also a former minister of defence, and the eight other accused were charged by the state in March with corruption involving millions of dollars and abuse of power.

"The Special Penal Code of the 1982 was a law that has no bearing to the current Ethiopian situation in which citizens enjoy a democratic constitution and an elected government," the defence lawyers said.

"The Dergue, the military junta that usurped power in Ethiopia in 1974, enacted the 1982 Special Penal Code to entrench dictatorship, to enable it conduct mass murder, torture and violate human rights," they added.
Tamirat was sacked as second-in-command in the government of Prime Minister Meles Zenawi last October and is held in "protective custody". The corruption trial was adjourned until May 30.
